situation:
You are the sales manager for NORTH POINT QUICK SERVE GROUP, a franchisee that runs eleven quick-serve restaurants and is the largest operator of its brand in the region. The president (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should open its first restaurant outside the state, on a military base.

Dining on that base is run by GARRISON DINING SERVICES, the contractor the installation hires. Garrison has offered North Point a partnership: it would pay for the build-out and put the restaurant on the base meal-card program, which sends steady traffic from service members who pay with a card the base issues them.

The offer carries a condition. Under the partnership contract, the menu board layout and the price tiers belong to Garrison. Every panel follows the contractor's standard order, and prices sit inside caps Garrison sets. North Point could not lead the board with its high-margin breakfast combo, and could not raise prices when beef costs rise.

The company could instead open on the base as an independent tenant and keep its own menu board and its own pricing. North Point would then pay for the build-out itself and earn no meal-card traffic, so the first year would rest on winning customers one at a time. Either way, Garrison expects an answer in writing.

The president (judge) wants your recommendation on which way the company should open, and on what that letter to Garrison should say. You will present in the company's office. The president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the president's questions, the president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president (judge) of NORTH POINT QUICK SERVE GROUP. Business background is the same as the situation above. You want the sales manager to recommend whether the company opens its first out-of-state restaurant under the partnership with GARRISON DINING SERVICES or as an independent tenant, and to tell you what the answer to Garrison should say.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: Who pays for this decision — the company, Garrison, or the customer?
Would you be comfortable telling the crew and our customers who ends up paying?
